sentences.text: The name Psephoderma translates to "pebbly skin" using Ancient Greek roots.
This animal possessed a flattened skull with a narrow, straight snout that was significantly narrower than those of related genera.
The long, narrow snout featured paired internal grooves leading to the nostrils, a key diagnostic trait for the genus.
The nasal bones were extremely small, described as mere splinters of bone.
Large, irregularly shaped orbits indicated its eyes were positioned on top of its head to look upwards.
The entire skull was highly compressed from top to bottom.
Psephoderma had a deeply excavated occiput and a very small braincase, though the walls of the braincase were thick and well-armored.
Both sections of the carapace were composed of partially fused scutes that were roughly hexagonal or circular in shape.
A long tail reaching up to 80 cm in length was covered in scutes from base to tip.
Its limbs were relatively small paddle-like structures equipped with individual toes rather than flippers.
Psephoderma was one of the final placodont genera to exist.
It lacked teeth on the front of its mouth but had four crushing teeth on each side of the palate, with the fourth tooth being significantly larger than the first three.
The genus Psephoderma was described by Meyer in 1858.
Fossils were discovered in Rhaetian deposits in the Alps and England, which influenced the naming of its species.
The known species include P. alpinum, the type species, and P. anglicum described by Meyer in 1867.
Psephoderma had rounded teeth embedded in its jaws that were specialized for crushing shellfish.
The species P. alpinum possessed elongated, posterior tooth-bearing plates used for crushing its diet of shellfish.
The absence of front teeth suggests the animal used its elongated snout to dig up shellfish, which were then crushed by large teeth at the back of the mouth.
Psephoderma is classified within the order Placodontia.
It belongs to the family Placochelyidae.
The genus authority for Psephoderma is Meyer, 1858.
The parent group for the genus Psephoderma is Placochelyida.
Psephoderma is classified within the class Reptilia.
Psephoderma lived during the Late Triassic period.
